chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan from Misma' from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hanan from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadeer, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every day?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, no.' He said: 'So how discourteous you are.' He said: 'Do you visit it every Friday?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit it every month?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit it every year?' I said, 'It may happen (in some years).'

He said: 'O Sadeer, how discourteous you are towards al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do you not know that for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two million angels, dishevelled and dusty, who weep and visit (the grave), not ceasing. And it is not difficult upon you, O Sadeer, to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) five times every week, and once every day.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, there are many farsakhs (travel distances) between us and him.'

So he said to me: 'Ascend to your roof, then turn right and left, then raise your head to the sky, then face towards the grave and say: 'As-salamu alayka ya Aba Abdillah, as-salamu alayka wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu' (Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah). A visitation (ziyarah) is written for you, and the visitation is equivalent to a Hajj and an Umrah.'
Sadeer said: 'So I used to do it in the month more than twenty times.'
ai.seo_question: How can one visit the grave of Imam al-Husayn if they live far away?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) laments the infrequency of visits by his companion Sadeer, contrasting human neglect with the ceaseless worship of a million angels. He introduces the concept of *ziyarat al-afdal* (superior visitation) for those distant from Karbala, demonstrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual accessibility of the Imams' graves regardless of geographical constraints. The promise that a single visitation equals both Hajj and Umrah underscores the immense spiritual merit attached to honoring the Ahl al-Bayt.
